# Nirodhavāra (Ya 3.2.2)

**ID:** Ya 3.2.2
**Section:** Yamaka (ya)
**Collection:** Abhidhamma
**Title (Pali):** Nirodhavāra
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh03m4.mul2.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Nirodhavāra* (Ya 3.2.2) constitutes the second division of the *Pavattivāra* (the section on the process or occurrence of phenomena) within the *Saccayamaka* ("Pairs on the Truths"), the third chapter of the *Yamaka* in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Anderson 1999]. While the preceding section addresses origination (*uppādavāra*), the *Nirodhavāra* provides a systematic dialectical analysis of cessation, interrogating how each of the four noble truths ceases in relation to the others across the three temporal periods of past, present, and future, with respect to persons and planes of rebirth [Nyanatiloka 2007; Anderson 1999].

Scholars note that the *Yamaka*'s structural analysis of phenomena across the threefold scheme of origination (*uppādavāra*), cessation (*nirodhavāra*), and origination-cessation (*uppādanirodhavāra*) exemplifies early Buddhist process metaphysics, which interprets experience through transient processes rather than enduring substances [Gal 2003; Ronkin 2005]. This analytical framework is functionally linked to the subdivision of a mental moment into distinct instants of arising (*uppādakkhaṇa*) and cessation or destruction (*bhaṅgakkhaṇa*), marking a pivotal stage in the doctrinal evolution toward a full theory of momentariness [Gal 2003; Ronkin 2005].

**Sources**

- [Anderson 1999] Carol S. Anderson, Pain and its Ending: The Four Noble Truths in the Theravāda Buddhist Canon (1999) — Description of the Pavattivāra and Nirodhavāra in the analysis of the noble truths across temporal divisions.
- [Gal 2003] Noa Gal, The Metaphysics of Experience: From the Buddha’s Teaching to the Abhidhamma (2003) — Analysis of the Yamaka process sections and the conceptual development of momentariness and sub-moments.
- [Nyanatiloka 2007] Nyanatiloka Mahāthera, Guide Through the Abhidhamma Piṭaka (1938, repr. 2007) — Structural outline of the Yamaka chapters and the Nirodhavāra analysis across past, present, and future.
- [Ronkin 2005] Noa Ronkin, Early Buddhist Metaphysics: The Making of a Philosophical Tradition (2005) — Discussion of Yamaka process metaphysics and the formulation of the cessation moment (bhaṅgakkhaṇa).
